title: Hand-built proof set from a compiled timeline, opened in the DAW (throwaway)
description:
## Intent

Prove the approach before specs: can a set assembled from a captured skeleton plus patched clip elements open and play in time?

## Steps

1. `apricity compile examples/march-blues.apr -o /tmp/march-blues.json` (timeline JSON).
2. A throwaway script in the session scratchpad (never committed) builds a set from `empty.als` plus one audio track per timeline track and one clip per event (warp markers from `Event.warp`, transpose from `semitones`, detune from `tuning_cents`, gain from `gain_db`), gzips it and references the sample files in place.
3. The owner opens it in the DAW: does it open, are clips on the grid, do the chords match `apricity render examples/march-blues.apr -o /tmp/mb.wav` by ear?
4. Record the outcome, every error dialog and every fix in comments, and the decision "template-and-patch" or "generate" in `design/daw-set.md`.

## Verification

Comment on this task with the DAW's reaction and an A/B listening note; `design/daw-set.md` has a "Decisions" entry for the approach.

## Release

No commit of the script. The design note change rides on the design-note task's commit.
